title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: E is a Q_ℓ-sheaf of rank n on Spec F_p. The words 'motif' (struck) and 'Q_ℓ-faisceau' (written above) are interchangeable here. Such an E is a finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-vector space with an action of the Frobenius f_E. Its L-function is L_E(t) = det(1 - f_E t)^{-1}. The page serves the local, point-level model of the functional equation of L-functions in the geometric case, which is the theme of cote 60.

Step 1, the dual. The dual E^∨ has Frobenius f_E^{-1} (transposed). Then det(1 - f^{-1} t) = det(f)^{-1} (-t)^n det(1 - f t^{-1}). Hence L_{E^∨}(t) = (-t)^{-n} det f_E · L_E(t^{-1}).

Step 2, purity. If E is pure of weight ρ (Weil conjectures), every eigenvalue has absolute value p^{ρ/2}. So det f_E = ε(E) p^{nρ/2} with ε = ±1. The sign depends only on the rank-one object ∧^n E = det E. He also notes that nρ/2 must be an integer: ρ odd forces n even, as with a symplectic pairing. Substituting gives L_{E^∨}(t) = ε(E) (-p^{ρ/2}/t)^n L_E(t^{-1}).

Step 3, self-duality. Suppose there is a perfect pairing E⊗E → Q_ℓ(-ρ); the qualifier is probably 'autodualité tensorielle', partly illegible. Then E^∨ ≅ E(ρ). Write * for the tensor product of L-series, L_E * L_F = L_{E⊗F}. Since L_{Q_ℓ(ρ)}(t) = 1/(1 - p^{-ρ} t), the Tate twist rescales the variable: L_{E^∨}(t) = L_{E(ρ)}(t) = L_E(t/p^ρ).

Combined (implicit) result: L_E(t/p^ρ) = ε(E) (-p^{ρ/2}/t)^n L_E(1/t). Equivalently, with t = p^{-s}, a relation s ↔ ρ - s. This is the elementary eigenvalue-level shadow of the functional equation of zeta functions of smooth projective varieties coming from Poincaré duality.
errors: The middle line L_{E^∨} = (L_E * L_{Q_ℓ(ρ)})^{-1} = (L_E * 1/(1-p^{-ρ}t))^{-1} = L_E * (1 - p^{-ρ}t) carries spurious inverses and does not literally make sense: L_{E⊗F} is not inverted, and tensoring with the virtual object -Q_ℓ(ρ) would give L_E(t/p^ρ)^{-1}. The final line L_{E^∨}(t) = L_E(t/p^ρ) is nevertheless correct, since E(ρ) has eigenvalues α p^{-ρ}. These are scratch slips.

The bracket describing ε(E) is incomplete and partly illegible. For ρ odd with a symplectic pairing, det f = p^{nρ/2} exactly (ε = +1). For ρ even the sign is the determinant of an orthogonal similitude and can be ±1. The page does not state this cleanly.

ideas.what: L-function of the dual of a lisse sheaf on a point: L_{E^∨}(t) = (-t)^{-n} det f · L_E(1/t)
ideas.modern_name: elementary characteristic-polynomial duality, the local functional equation at a point
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard linear algebra; SGA 4½ / SGA 5 context (Grothendieck, Deligne)
ideas.where_published: SGA 5 (exposés on L-functions) / Grothendieck's Bourbaki talk 279 (1964), in substance

ideas.what: det Frob = ±p^{nρ/2} for a pure sheaf of weight ρ, with the parity constraint ρ odd ⇒ n even and the sign governed by det E
ideas.modern_name: sign of the functional equation / determinant of a self-dual pure representation

ideas.what: A self-dual pure E of weight ρ satisfies E^∨ ≅ E(ρ), so L_{E^∨}(t) = L_E(t/p^ρ), giving L_E(t/p^ρ) = ε(-p^{ρ/2}/t)^n L_E(1/t)
ideas.modern_name: functional equation from Poincaré duality / Tate twist
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, Formule de Lefschetz et rationalité des fonctions L (Sém. Bourbaki 279); SGA 4½ 'Rapport'

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine scratch computations of the eigenvalue-level functional equation for a pure, self-dual Frobenius module over F_p. All of it is standard and well documented in the literature.
transcription_corrections: First formula: the exponent is (-t)^{-n}, not (-t)^{n}.
Second L-formula: it reads ε(E)(-p^{ρ/2}/t)^n L_E(t^{-1}); the t is in the denominator, not (-p^{ρ/2} t)^n.
'motif ∧E' should be read as ∧^n E = det E (maximal exterior power).
The struck 'dans' in line 1 is probably 'on'/'dans' crossed out before 'on trouve donc'; immaterial.
